history.origins: Tres y Dos is a folk rummy-style game played across the Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Puerto Rico. Contributors report that most Dominicans who have ever played cards know the game; it is often learned in childhood. In Cuba, children sometimes bet marbles on each hand while adults may play for money. The game has no formal documented history; it is transmitted informally as a household and social pastime.
timeline: 20th century: Folk game played in Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Puerto Rico.

setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards each. Stock + Discard pile.

rules.objective: Form a 'Tres y Dos' (Full House: 3 of a kind + 2 of a kind).
rules.gameplay: 1. Draw (Stock or Discard). 2. Discard. Cannot return same card taken from discard. First to complete wins.

strategy.basic: Collect pairs and trips. Keep flexible cards.
strategy.advanced: Block opponents by holding their needed cards.

scoring.description: No scoring. First to complete wins the round.
scoring.winCondition: Form a 'Tres y Dos' (Full House: 3 of a kind + 2 of a kind).
